title: The Missing Notebook

beats.narrativeText: The learner discovers references to one final field notebook belonging to Dr. Elara Quinn.
Only scattered pages of the notebook remain, and much of its content is missing.
The learner combines journal entries, maps, timestamps and previous discoveries to begin reassembling the notebook.
Arranging the surviving pages chronologically begins to reveal Dr. Quinn's final recorded observations.
The learner must write the missing sections using the available evidence, distinguishing confirmed facts from reasonable inference.
beats.trigger: Missing sections written and inference separated from fact

beats.narrativeText: The reconstructed notebook confirms that the expedition was attempting to protect important scientific discoveries — not hide them.
The learner reflects on how much can be understood even from a badly damaged record.
Dr. Quinn's motivations become clear, and the campaign transitions from investigation toward solving the expedition mystery.

activities.title: Reassemble Notebook Pages
activities.storyContext: Only scattered pages remain of Dr. Elara Quinn's final field notebook.
activities.instructions: Read the surviving notebook pages and work out how they fit together.
activities.output: A reassembled order of the surviving notebook pages.

activities.title: Arrange Events Chronologically
activities.storyContext: Journal entries, maps, timestamps and previous discoveries all hold clues to the correct order of events.
activities.instructions: Arrange the events described in the notebook into chronological order.
activities.output: A chronological timeline of Dr. Quinn's final observations.

activities.title: Write Missing Sections Using Evidence
activities.storyContext: Large parts of the notebook are missing entirely.
activities.instructions: Write the missing sections of the notebook, using evidence from the surviving pages and previous discoveries.
activities.output: Written reconstructions of the missing notebook sections.

activities.title: Distinguish Facts From Inference
activities.storyContext: Not everything written in the reconstructed notebook can be fully trusted.
activities.instructions: Sort your reconstruction into confirmed facts and reasonable inference.
activities.output: Two lists: confirmed facts and reasonable inference.

activities.title: Write Another Perspective
activities.storyContext: Every expedition member would have experienced these events differently to Dr. Quinn.
activities.instructions: Write an additional journal entry from the perspective of another expedition member.
activities.output: A journal entry written from another expedition member's perspective.

activities.title: Reconstructing Incomplete Manuscripts
activities.storyContext: Reconstructing this notebook is similar to real historical research.
activities.instructions: Find out how archaeologists and historians reconstruct incomplete manuscripts.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What do you think Dr. Quinn was really trying to protect?

discussionPoints: What do you think Dr. Quinn was protecting, and why?
How did you decide what to write in the missing sections?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for missing sections that are reasonably supported by surrounding evidence, and a clear separation between confirmed facts and inference.

completionCriteria: Notebook pages reassembled, events arranged chronologically, and missing sections written using evidence.
